column1: # entry parameter is, in each context the game calls it from.
# A buffer parameter names an allocation in the generated buffers.tsv; `state`
# names `core_state`, the ONE buffer every scalar field lives in; an index
# parameter (`i_*`) names the scalar field whose slot it is, and `use` says
# whether the entry only reads that cell (`in`) or writes it (`inout`).
# tests/doom-core/source-registry.rb checks every row against the contract, the
# generated layout and registry.h, and access.tsv's doom_core_render row.
# Three other spellings, only where the original has no resident field:
#   none           the context passes no buffer (count 0)
#   arg:NAME       no resident field: a buffer the lane fills from the caller's
#                  argument NAME at each call (the status bar's ammo, maxammo,
#                  weaponowned) -- the hand-off at the call site
#   job:NAME       a field of the queued job record, which the jobs rings hold;
#                  the lane hands the record's two cells over in a buffer of their own
#   derived:WHAT   a table of slot indices the lane reads off the original
